notes:
40 stations, numbered 81 to 120, under the heading "West Coast of Scotland". It has three sub-headings: "Mainland" (81-82), "Outer Hebrides" (83-88) and "Mainland, Skye, and Inner Hebrides" (89-120). In the coast field I wrote these as "West Coast of Scotland--<sub-heading>". The Isle of Man stations (116-120) come under the last sub-heading, as printed. No row gives a light's character, so character is null everywhere.

Conventions:
- Fragments have leading indentation removed. Spacing inside each line is kept exactly.
- Name and place keep the punctuation printed after them (for example "Rona," / "Skye."), following your "Farn, Inner," example.
- For keepers I dropped the full stop that ends each row ("John M'Gill." becomes "John M'Gill"), following your "J. B. Smith" example.
- The numbers are printed with a full stop after them ("81."). I recorded them without it.
- other holds the height column. Only Cape Wrath prints its unit ("400 ft."); the other heights are bare numbers in feet.

Rows to check:
- 86 Monach Island: two heights are printed in a brace, "{ Upper 150 }" / "{ Lower  62 }", with the second on line 2956. I treated the brace as belonging to the heights, not as a station mark.
- 93 Hynish Signal Tower, Tiree and 94 Skerryvore, off Tiree: a brace joins the two rows. The height 150 and keeper William Crow are printed only on the Hynish line, so I put them only on 93. The brace probably means they apply to both (Hynish was the shore signal station for Skerryvore). Neither row has a return mark.
- 99 Fladda, Easdale and 101 M'Arthur's Head, Islay: each has a * and is also in italics. By the key, these contradict each other (italics means no return this year), so one of the two is probably a printing slip. I recorded both marks as "*, italic".
- 119 Bahama Bank: "1880.--" means a station added this year. The type "(L.V.)" and the ‡ (see the light-vessel footnote) are recorded. "--" stands in the height column, and the keeper is printed only as the surname "Johns."
- 120 Langness: "1880.--" means added this year. "Lighthouse" is part of the printed name, so I left type null. The place is "do." (ditto, meaning Isle of Man), kept as printed.
- Rows with no keeper and no mark (88, 89, 97, 105, 106, 118, 120) sent no return.

Spellings that look odd, kept as printed:
- "Rosspire" (row 90): probably a misprint for Ross-shire.
- "Island Glass": Eilean Glas.
- "Rhu Stoir": Rhu Stoer.
- "Dhuheartach": Dubh Artach.
- "Rhuvaal": Rhuvaal / Rubh' a' Mhail.
- "Lochindaul": Loch Indaal.
- "Chickens Rock" is printed without an apostrophe.
- "Argyleshire".
